*StarHub: Discussions Continuing; No Certainty or Assurance of Deal
StarHub in Talks to Acquire Keppel's M1

Singapore's StarHub is in talks with Keppel Ltd. to acquire its M1 unit, months after a proposed $1.1 billion acquisition of the telecommunications company by another rival fell through amid regulatory scrutiny.
StarHub and Keppel confirmed the talks in separate statements late Wednesday, after a news report said that StarHub is in talks with Keppel over an M1 deal.
Keppel, an asset manager and operator, said it is continuing to explore consolidation opportunities involving M1, as it believes consolidation is needed for Singapore's telco sector.

"These discussions are ongoing and there is no certainty or assurance whatsoever that these discussions will progress beyond the current stage or that any transaction in respect of [M1] will arise," said StarHub, a telecom operator.

The talks comes after Australia-listed Tuas said in May that a deal to acquire M1 was off, amid allegations that its Simba Telecom unit may have used unauthorized radio frequency bands, potentially breaching Singapore's Telecommunications Act and the conditions of its operating license. Tuas said then that its agreement to buy M1 from Keppel had been terminated.
In August 2025, Keppel agreed to sell its entire 83.9% stake in M1 to Tuas's Simba subsidiary.
